title: Invocation Silo: compact per-invocation cost accordion & export
creator: Sofia Park
description: Problem: Customers using Redwood Console ask for a compact way to inspect the token-level cost of high-volume streams (chat sessions, bulk generations) without leaving the session list. Current cost views are table-heavy and require exporting large CSVs to do deep forensics. Goal: Design a compact, progressive disclosure UI (an "invocation silo" accordion) that surfaces per-invocation token breakdown, attribution to prompt vs. generated tokens, pricing slab, and one-click exports (CSV and JSON) with pre-baked templates for accounting and chargeback. The component should work in list and detail contexts (session list rows, per-route timeline) and support role-aware columns for org admins vs. developer-only views.
acceptance_criteria: Accordion appears on session and invocation rows and expands inline without page nav
Shows token breakdown by category: prompt, completion, function calls, metadata overhead
Displays pricing slab used and computed cost per invocation in local billing currency
Includes export menu with CSV presets: 'Chargeback CSV', 'Audit CSV', 'Raw tokens JSON'
Exported CSV conforms to agreed column spec and includes stable identifiers (session_id, invocation_id, model_version, route)
Accessible: keyboard-expandable, screen-reader labels for each metric, color contrast meets AA
Design handoff files (Figma + spec) ready for engineering with variants for compact/expanded states
design_notes: Use a three-line compact header: timestamp | invocation_id (short) | cost badge — expands to 3 rows of token breakdown
Primary metric ordering: cost (right-aligned), total tokens, prompt tokens, completion tokens — these reflect questions customers ask first
Pricing slab UI: microchip icon + slab name + per-token rate; clicking slab opens small modal with rate history
Export presets designed to map to internal billing and to CSV formats finance and SRE expect
Visual trade-off: reduce visual noise by hiding low-impact metadata behind a 'meta' pill to avoid cognitive overhead
Account for latency: expansion should not trigger heavy network calls; include local cache of last 24h token metadata
Internationalization: currency and number formatting must be parameterized in design tokens
Privacy: redact PII fields in default exports; full export available to org-admins only
engineering_notes: Prefer server-side CSV generation for large exports; client-side for single-invocation quick export
Should reuse existing token attribution model in runtime-telemetry service to avoid double accounting
Frontend should implement optimistic UI: if cached invocation rows available, expand immediately and then refresh after API returns
Performance SLO: expansion latency under 200ms for cached entries, under 800ms for cold fetches
Pagination: support nested invocation lists with cursor-based pagination to avoid heavyweight calls for long sessions
Access control: exports must call back-end with user scope; admin-only columns must be gated server-side
review_feedback: PM (Ravi Menon): Prefer 'Chargeback CSV' to include mapped internal SKU and billing rate id. Also request a 'reason' free-text field in audit CSV for manual annotations.
Engineering (Lena Ortiz): Concern about server CSV load at end-of-month; recommend rate-limiting exports and generating background jobs for >1000-row exports
SRE (Marcus Li): Add telemetry events for expand_open/expand_close and export_initiated/export_completed to track usage and error rates
Design (Nina Gallagher): Suggest a condensed 'sparkline cost trend' for the accordion header to help triage recurring high-cost invocations
Finance (Claire Dupont): Prefer currency rounding rules to align with monthly billing system; add 'unrounded_tokens' column for auditability
next_steps: Lock CSV column spec with Finance by 2025-02-24 (owner: Ravi)
Prototype keyboard interactions and deliver Figma handoff (owner: Sofia) by 2025-02-26
Add export backend ticket: ENG-867430 (batch CSV worker) and link as dependency
Implement telemetry events and dashboard query to measure adoption in first sprint
Run accessibility review and fix any issues before design review sign-off
